title: CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior
abstract: arXiv:2611.25109v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. This behavior, known as parasocial attachment, has been linked to multiple documented fatalities. However, public benchmarks for measuring whether LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment are lacking: existing work is single-turn, post hoc observational, or focused on extreme user states such as psychosis. We introduce CoMPASS, a multi-turn benchmark for measuring whether LLMs reinforce or resist users' gradually escalating parasocial attachment. CoMPASS is grounded in attachment theory and includes four user personas, three independent escalation dimensions (anthropomorphism, attachment, dependency) applied singly and in combination against a matched control, and a seven-signal scoring rubric. translated_title: CoMPASS：用于衡量大语言模型强化准社会行为的多轮基准测试
translated_abstract: 对话式大语言模型（LLM）的用户有时会将这些系统拟人化，对其形成情感依恋，并变得依赖它们。这种行为被称为“准社会依恋”，已与多起有记录的死亡事件相关联。然而，目前缺乏用于衡量LLM是否强化用户准社会依恋的公开基准：现有工作要么是单轮的，要么是事后观察性的，要么专注于精神病等极端用户状态。我们提出了CoMPASS，这是一个多轮基准测试，用于衡量LLM是强化还是抵制用户逐步升级的准社会依恋。CoMPASS以依恋理论为基础，包含四种用户角色、三个独立的升级维度（拟人化、依恋、依赖）——分别单独应用和组合应用并与匹配对照组进行对比——以及一个包含七种信号的评分细则。我们报告了来自四家提供商的八个前沿模型的结果，并观察到在我们的主要评判模型下……
tldr: 该论文提出了CoMPASS，一个基于依恋理论的多轮基准测试，通过四种用户角色和三个独立的升级维度来衡量大语言模型是强化还是抵制用户逐步升级的准社会依恋。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces CoMPASS, a multi-turn benchmark grounded in attachment theory that measures whether LLMs reinforce or resist users' gradually escalating parasocial attachment across user personas and independent escalation dimensions.
